prompt:

Begin your answer with exactly one line: "Verdict: yes", "Verdict: no", or "Verdict: cannot tell from this trace". Then answer the question.
answer:
Verdict: no

## File-call latency

Across the whole trace (offsets **0–30,632.7 ms**), file calls were not materially slow and none of the measured calls had a long tail:

| Call | Count | Median | P90 | P99 | Maximum |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `openat` | 6,303 | 0.011 ms | 0.016 ms | 0.020 ms | 0.064 ms |
| `rename` | 6,000 | 0.014 ms | 0.019 ms | 0.020 ms | 0.393 ms |
| `unlink` | 6,001 | 0.011 ms | 0.013 ms | 0.016 ms | 0.395 ms |
| `write` | 6,006 | 0.005 ms | 0.006 ms | 0.008 ms | 0.159 ms |
| `pread64` | 298 | 0.004 ms | 0.005 ms | 0.007 ms | 0.029 ms |
| `lseek` | 298 | 0.001 ms | 0.001 ms | 0.001 ms | 0.001 ms |
| `newfstatat` | 33 | 0.005 ms | 0.005 ms | 0.011 ms | 0.011 ms |

The writer spent **0.8%** of its time in file-system calls and **0.1%** in storage I/O calls; the reader spent **0.009%** and **0.004%**, respectively. The occasional higher `rename`/`unlink`/`write` maximums do not change the overall result: the measured calls have **no long tail**.
